s: The global origin of Environmental Impact Assessment is linked to the National Environmental Policy Act of which country and year?
x: The global origin of EIA is associated with the United States National Environmental Policy Act, enacted in 1969.

s: When did the Planning Commission ask the Department of Science and Technology to examine river-valley projects?
x: India's EIA process began in 1976-77 when the Planning Commission asked DST to examine river-valley projects.

s: Through which amendment was a public hearing made mandatory under the 1994 EIA framework?
x: Mandatory public hearing was added by the 1997 amendment to the 1994 framework.

s: The EIA Notification, 2006 made environmental clearance compulsory for how many project categories?
x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.

s: In which year was India's first EIA Notification under the Environment (Protection) Act issued on 27 January?
x: The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994; earlier clearance was only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.

s: Under the EIA framework, when must environmental clearance be obtained as a rule?
o: After an environmental audit finds non-compliance
Only for products assessed through LCA
x: Prior environmental clearance is mandatory; post-facto approval, where recognised at all, is only a narrow exception.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Environmental Impact Assessment identifies, predicts and evaluates the environmental impacts of development projects.
R2 Code of Practices is a framework for environmentally responsible electronics recycling.
R2 Code of Practices is another name for Environmental Impact Assessment.
EIA assesses the likely environmental consequences of a proposed project or activity before implementation.
x: Option C is incorrect: R2 is a code for responsible electronics recycling. EIA is the process of assessing a project's likely environmental impact before it starts.

s: In which year was EIA first used in India?
x: EIA was first used in 1978, after the 1976-77 DST review of river-valley projects.

s: To which of the following does the R2 Code of Practices relate?
x: R2 Code of Practices is not EIA; it is for responsible electronics recycling.

s: On which date was the EIA Notification, 2006 issued?
x: The EIA Notification of 14 September 2006 replaced the first notification of 27 January 1994.

o: EIA focuses only on product design, while LCA focuses on project location
EIA and LCA both focus only on air pollution levels

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: What is EIA (Environmental Impact Assessment)?
o: Studying environmental effects of a project

s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.

s: Which of the following pairs (tool – scope) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Environmental audit – A project evaluated before it starts
Life-Cycle Assessment – A product or process across its whole life cycle
Environmental Impact Assessment – A project evaluated before it starts
Cumulative Impact Assessment – Combined effect of several projects in one area
x: An environmental audit is a compliance check of an operating unit after the fact; evaluation before a project starts is EIA.

s: Who formulated the 12 principles of green chemistry?
x: The 12 principles of green chemistry (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, renewable feedstocks, design for degradation) were set out by Anastas and Warner in 1998. The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development; Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962); the Club of Rome issued Limits to Growth (1972).

s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.

s: Which of the following describes cleaner production?
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.

s: On which of the following does Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA) focus?
o: A specific project before it starts
A product or process from cradle to grave
x: LCA covers a product's life cycle; EIA covers a project, SEA policies and an audit a running unit.

s: Which tool checks the compliance of a running unit after the fact?
x: An environmental audit assesses compliance of a running unit after the fact.

s: Which tool assesses the combined effect of several projects in one area?
x: Cumulative Impact Assessment examines the combined effect of several projects in one area.

s: Database is
o: A collection of information that can only be retrieved
An organized collection of data that can be manipulated or retrieved
A collection of only numeric data that can be manipulated and retrieved
A backup storage where data can be saved

s: Which EIA stage identifies key issues and sets the Terms of Reference?
x: Scoping fixes key issues and Terms of Reference; screening decides whether EIA is needed and appraisal evaluates the final report.

s: Which is the first stage of the EIA process?
x: The EIA sequence is screening, scoping, appraisal and decision.

s: Which of the following pairs (EIA stage – what happens) is correctly matched?
o: Monitoring – Clearance granted with conditions or rejected
Decision – Implementation of the EMP is checked
Appraisal – Expert committee evaluates the EIA report
Appraisal – Clearance granted with conditions or rejected
x: At appraisal the expert committee evaluates the EIA report; at decision clearance is granted or rejected, and monitoring checks EMP implementation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EIA project categories?
o: Category B projects are appraised by the central Expert Appraisal Committee
Category B projects are cleared by SEIAA
Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC
Category A projects are cleared by MoEFCC
x: Category B projects are appraised by the State Expert Appraisal Committee and cleared by SEIAA; the central EAC appraises Category A.

s: At which stage of the EIA process are alternatives compared?
x: Impact prediction includes comparison of alternatives; baseline data surveys the existing environment and mitigation planning includes the EMP.

s: Implementation of the Environment Management Plan is checked at which EIA stage?
x: Monitoring, the last stage, checks implementation of the EMP.

s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, which of the following is true of Category B2 projects?
o: Require a full EIA by MoEFCC
Are appraised by the central EAC
x: Category B1 projects require an EIA while B2 projects do not; both fall under state-level appraisal and clearance.

s: What is the status of the Draft EIA Notification, 2020?
o: Praised for longer public consultation periods than 2006
Notable for abolishing penalties for violations
Not finalised, and criticised for proposing post-facto clearance
x: The 2020 draft was not finalised and was contested, particularly for post-facto clearance and shorter consultation periods.

s: Under the Draft EIA Notification, 2020, who alone could report violations?
x: The draft restricted reporting of violations to the violator or the government, one of its contested provisions.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, who clears Category A projects?
x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 1994, in which Schedule were projects needing MoEF clearance listed?
x: Under the 1994 notification, Schedule I projects needed MoEF clearance.

s: Under the Draft EIA Notification, 2020, the notice period for a public hearing was proposed to be cut from 30 days to how many days?
x: The draft 2020 notification proposed cutting the public hearing notice from 30 to 20 days, one of its contested points.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, which category of projects is appraised by the SEAC and needs an EIA report?
x: B1 projects are appraised by SEAC and need an EIA; B2 projects need no EIA; Category A goes to the central EAC.

s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, within how many days must a public hearing be completed?
x: The hearing notice must be given at least 30 days in advance and the hearing completed within 45 days.

s: In the EIA process, who decides whether a project is 'strategic' and thus exempt from public hearing?
x: The Central Government decides 'strategic' status (criticised as arbitrary); the SPCB only conducts the public hearing.

s: Which of the following is NOT exempt from an EIA public hearing?
x: Defence, strategic, B2 and industrial-estate units are exempt; Category A projects are not.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, what is the minimum notice for a public hearing?
x: Notice must be at least 30 days; the 2020 draft proposed cutting it to 20 days.

s: An APPCB public hearing in May 2026, where the draft EIA was called error-ridden, was on a Water Aerodrome at which site?
x: The hearing concerned a Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage, Vijayawada.

x: SAEIA is the backup for SEIAA, while SCEIA is the backup for SEAC.

x: Members serve 3-4 years, at most two terms, with an age limit of 70.

Permitting post-facto clearances as a routine measure
Creation of an independent EIA authority

s: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) came into force in:
x: The National Green Tribunal has been established on 18 October, 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act 2010, for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to the environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources including enforcement of any legal rights relating to environment. The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), a statutory organization was constituted in September 1974 under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974. Principal functions of the CPCB are (i) to promote cleanliness of streams and wells in different areas of the States by prevention, control and abatement of water pollution, and (ii) to improve the quality of air and to prevent, control or abate air pollution in the country. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

s: National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established by the Government of India in:

s:
How is the National Green Tribunal (NGT) different from Central Pollution Control Board (CDCB)

I. The NGT has been established by an ACt, whereas the CPCB has been created by an executive order of the Government.

II. The NGT provides environmental Justice and helps reduce the burden of litigation in the higher courts whereas CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells, and aims to improve the quality of air in the country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement I is wrong because the CPCB is a statutory body created under the Water Act 1974, not by an executive order. Statement II is right because the NGT gives environmental justice and eases the litigation burden on higher courts, while the CPCB sets standards and monitors.

s: What is the nature of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Statutory body with powers similar to a civil court
Executive body with only advisory jurisdiction
Constitutional body with only administrative powers
x: The NGT is a statutory, not constitutional, body with civil-court powers in matters within its jurisdiction.

s: The establishment of the National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to constitutional remedies under Article 32
x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.

s: Within how many days does an appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lie to the Supreme Court?
x: An appeal against an NGT order may be filed before the Supreme Court within 90 days.

s: When was the National Green Tribunal set up?
x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010, the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and it started functioning in July 2011.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal is incorrect?
o: The NGT was established on October 18, 2010.
The constitutional anchor of the NGT is Article 28.
Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was the first Chairperson of the NGT.
The NGT was established under the NGT Act, 2010.
x: Option B is incorrect: the NGT's constitutional basis is Article 21 (the right to life, read to include a healthy environment), not Article 28. Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was its first chair.

s: Which of the following is a zonal bench location of the National Green Tribunal?
x: Pune is a zonal bench; New Delhi hosts the Principal Bench and Jodhpur and Shillong are circuit benches.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
x: Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was the first NGT Chairperson; Justice Prakash Shrivastava is the current one.

s: Besides the Chairperson, how many Judicial and Expert Members does the National Green Tribunal have?
x: The NGT has a Chairperson with 10 to 20 Judicial and 10 to 20 Expert Members.

s: Which of the following is a circuit bench, not a zonal bench, of the National Green Tribunal?
x: Jodhpur, Shimla and Shillong are circuit benches; Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai are zonal benches.

s: When did the National Green Tribunal start functioning?
x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010, the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and it started functioning in July 2011.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Green Tribunal?
o: It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
It is bound by all the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure
It follows the principles of natural justice
Its principal bench is at New Delhi
x: The NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it is guided by the principles of natural justice.

s: After which two countries did India become the third country to set up a specialised environmental tribunal?
x: With the NGT in 2010, India became the third country with a specialised environmental tribunal, after Australia and New Zealand.

s: On which date was the National Green Tribunal Act passed?
x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010; the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and began work in July 2011.

s: Who is qualified to be appointed Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
o: A judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court
An environmental scientist with 15 years' experience
x: The Chairperson is a judge of the Supreme Court or Chief Justice of a High Court; in practice a retired SC judge.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal as of 2026?
x: Justice Prakash Shrivastava heads the NGT; Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was its first Chairperson.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

s: Why was the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 distinctive?

Establishment of the Central Pollution Control Board
x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of accidents involving hazardous substances.

s: The NGT combines which two roles associated earlier with separate environmental institutions?
o: Original jurisdiction over environmental disputes and the appellate role of the NEAA
x: The NGT combines original jurisdiction over environmental disputes with the appellate role earlier performed by the NEAA.

s: Which body took over the role of the National Environment Appellate Authority set up under its 1997 Act?
x: The NEAA no longer exists in its original form; its role passed to the NGT.

x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was never brought into force and was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.

s: How many Acts are listed in Schedule I of the NGT Act, under the Tribunal's jurisdiction?
x: Seven Acts, from the Water Act 1974 to the Biological Diversity Act 2002, are in Schedule I.

s: Which of the following Acts is within the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
x: The Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 is in Schedule I; the Wildlife Act 1972 and the Forest Rights Act 2006 are outside the NGT.

s: What was the National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 meant to hear?

s: In January 2022, the National Green Tribunal constituted a mission on which of the following?

s: In which year was the National Environment Appellate Authority Act passed?
x: The NEAA Act, 1997 dealt with appeals against environmental clearances; the National Environment Tribunal Act came in 1995.
